info.name: Khoj - CORS and reachability
info.description:
Diagnoses a browser 'Failed to fetch' between the Vercel frontend and the Render backend.

READ THIS FIRST

Postman cannot reproduce a CORS failure. CORS is enforced by the browser, not the server: the server always answers, and the browser decides whether the page is allowed to read the answer. Postman is not a browser, so it ignores Access-Control-Allow-Origin entirely and every request below will succeed even if a real page would be blocked.

What this collection is for is the other half of the job: proving what the server actually sends, so you can tell a genuine CORS rejection apart from DNS failure, a refused connection, a sleeping instance or a wrong VITE_API_URL - all four of which surface in the console as the same useless 'Failed to fetch'.

Run the folder top to bottom. If every test passes, the server side is correct and the fault is in the browser: an extension blocking the request, mixed content, or a stale bundle. See request 7 for how to confirm that in the browser itself.

variable.description: The Render service. No trailing slash.
Exactly what the browser puts in the Origin header: scheme + host + port, no trailing slash, no path.

item.name: 1. Is the backend reachable at all?

exec: // Rules out DNS failure, a refused connection and a sleeping instance.
// If this fails, nothing below is meaningful and the problem is not CORS.
// A cold Render instance takes tens of seconds to wake. That looks like a
// hang in the browser, which people report as a CORS error.
pm.test('answered promptly (not waking from sleep)', function () {
// The request the browser sends before any POST carrying an Authorization
// header. If this is wrong, the real request is never sent at all and the
// console shows 'Failed to fetch' with no server log to match it.
// Byte-identical, not merely present. A trailing slash or a path here is
// the single most common cause of this whole failure.
pm.test('Allow-Origin exactly matches the Origin sent', function () {
// Every request from the app carries a Firebase ID token. If this header
// is not allowed, every authenticated call fails while anonymous ones work.
// With credentials enabled the server may not answer '*'. The two settings
// are only valid together when the origin is echoed explicitly.
pm.expect(allowed, 'wildcard origin is illegal with credentials').to.not.eql('*');
